newsitem.title: CANADA: IPL plans with Noverco well on track - CEO.
newsitem.headline: IPL plans with Noverco well on track - CEO.

text.p: IPL Energy Inc, having sealed a deal to buy into Quebec natural gas holding company Noverco Inc, is well on its way to becoming Canada's first big player in the brave new world of one-stop-shopping in energy services, IPL Chief Executive Brian MacNeill said on Wednesday.

The C$330-million deal also provides IPL with a platform for future investments in other natural gas and electricity interests in Canada and the United States, MacNeill said in an interview at the company's Calgary headquarters.

"What we are moving towards is really taking the strengths of what we have, which is a strong delivery component and moving it into more of an energy services complement," he said. "This is a logical alliance. Noverco certainly is a big distributor in Quebec. There's a good mix of expertise coming together between ourselves and Hydro-Quebec in a number of fields."

Under the deal announced on Tuesday, IPL will join government-owned electric utility Hydro-Quebec and Gaz de France as a 32-percent owner of Noverco, whose main asset is an 80-percent stake in Quebec gas distribution concern Gaz Metropolitain and Co LP.
It will also issue eight percent of its own stock to Noverco for proceeds of C$287 million and give it an option to boost the stake to 10 percent next year.

The move was the culmination of three months of negotiations with Noverco partners, especially Hydro-Quebec, whose chairman, Andre Caille, has often articulated his plans to make the huge utility a major North American energy player.
Highest on Caille's wish list was a big out-of-province partner with a strong distribution business, MacNeill said.

The deal was the latest of several announced by IPL in the last few months inside and outside of its traditional regulated pipeline business. The speed at which IPL brought its strategy to fruition surpised analysts.
"If you would have looked at us a year ago, we were basically a liquids pipeline company," MacNeill said.
"Now we've got some gas distribution expertise, we've obviously got some electrical distribution expertise, we've got some retail distribution expertise."
On the retail side, the company hopes to eventually be a major provider of suites of gas, electricity and even water services to individual homes, he said.
The concept of "convergence" in energy services has been front and center in the deregulating U.S. market for the past few years with companies like Enron Corp and NGC Corp at the forefront.
The U.S. experience provided a good guide for Canadian companies, which are boosting their presence south of the border, MacNeill said.

Other Canadian firms such as TransCanada PipeLines Ltd and Westcoast Energy Inc, like IPL once considered pure utilities known strictly for their yield to investors, are moving into various non-regulated North American energy ventures, he said.

Next on IPL's agenda will be to branch out with investments in eastern Canadian and Northeast U.S. electric utilities, where IPL's distribution and Hydro-Quebec's electricity know-how will mean new and diversified revenues, MacNeill said.

He said he was not surprised by the warm stock market reception to the Noverco deal -- seen boosting IPL's earnings per share by 12 cents annually -- as it represented the completion of plans communicated to investors for months.
IPL shares in Toronto climbed 1.55 to 49.40 in busy trade late in Wednesday's session. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
